title: Do Barkley's transitional-pipe-flow puffs, extended to 2D with a label they copy, give a birth-death population (stochastic splits and decays) on which heredity and selection can act without any written division rule?
summary: Barkley's two-field model (PRE 2011; 20261027T1234-c55-literature) has localized turbulent puffs q on a mean-flow field u that split and decay stochastically, with the two rates crossing at a critical parameter (directed percolation). Neither the model nor the advective-excitable class is in the ledger. Its puffs are discrete, advected, self-sustaining structures whose births and deaths come from the dynamics, which is what C:open-ended and the heredity rungs need.
experiment: One loop. World: the continuous model q_t + U q_x = q(u + r - 1 - (r + delta)(q - 1)^2) + Dq lap q + sigma q xi, u_t + U u_x = eps1 (1 - u) - eps2 u q - u_x (+ Du lap u), eps1 0.04, eps2 0.2, delta 0.1, on a periodic 2D strip (e.g. 512 x 64) so puffs are localized in x and y; noise sigma on q makes splits and decays stochastic. Screen r for the window where single puffs both split and decay (labkit counts of splits and of tracks that end without children). Then add a label copied where q is high (dl/dt = k q l (1 - l) - d l + advection), every puff labelled at t0 and a trait-blind swap mutation; give one label kind a small change in r and run it against the identical-draw twin (as in 20261027T0222-c49-thermals-selection-claim). Pass: puffs from a noisy initial field, >= 20 persistent splits per run, daughters keep the label, and the favoured kind's share rises against the twin on 2 seeds.
